generalized_learning.generalized_failure_pattern: A candidate can be functionally green and carry a valid-looking handoff while current base drift makes the pull request unmergeable.
generalized_learning.plausible_wrong_implementation: Freeze and hand off a green head without rechecking PR mergeability against the current base immediately before release readiness.
trigger_signals: base branch advanced after material validation
pull request mergeability changed to dirty/conflicting
handoff was produced from an older base SHA
generalized_learning.reusable_control: Before terminal handoff, read fresh PR identity and require mergeable=true against the current base; if dirty/conflicting, reconcile, rerun gates and refreeze.
generalized_learning.prevention_rule: Terminal readiness must be based on current base identity, not only exact-head CI.
generalized_learning.detection_rule: Fail handoff readiness when fresh PR mergeability is false/dirty or base SHA differs from the base used by the frozen candidate without reconciliation.

transfer_cases.scenario: A synthetic PR is green but base advances into a textual conflict before handoff.
A certificate names an older base while the live PR is no longer mergeable.

skill_changes.evidence: Current delivery now treats fresh PR/base mergeability as a terminal structural control.
NEG-PR-MERGEABILITY is carried into inherited controls and risk saturation for subsequent re-audit.
